# Decomposition frames

## Component tree
Use when knowledge is still shallow. List major elements, then reorganize until the structure becomes explanatory.

## Deductive driver tree
Use when relationships are known mathematically or causally. Example: revenue = price × volume; profit = revenue − cost.

## Hypothesis tree
Use once there is enough context to state likely explanations. Each branch is a falsifiable claim and implies a test.

## Decision tree
Use for sequential choices and uncertainty. Make decision gates explicit.

## Business performance frames
Useful starting points include:
- Revenue: price × volume × mix × retention / expansion dynamics
- Costs: fixed vs variable; COGS vs operating expense
- Unit economics: acquisition, gross margin, retention, payback
- ROIC: margin × capital turnover
- Growth: existing customers / new customers / new products / new markets

## Root-cause frame
Start from observed outcome → proximate drivers → root causes. Use 5 Whys carefully; stop when the next “why” no longer yields an actionable or testable cause.

## Alternative framing test
Before committing, try at least two different ways to cut the problem. Prefer the frame that produces the most testable hypotheses and decision-relevant analysis.
